key_insight: A large-deformation viscoelastic model captures the rate-sensitive, coupled volumetric and distortional response of an open-cell elastomeric foam.
engineering_relevance: The model supports finite-element prediction of foam behavior for impact protection and cushioning applications.
method: Combine an equilibrium hyperelastic response with nonlinear Maxwell-like viscoelastic contributions.
Use logarithmic-strain invariants to represent large deformations and volumetric–distortional coupling.
Calibrate against compression and tension data at decade-spaced strain rates, with localization screening.
evidence_signal: Predictions for intentionally inhomogeneous validation tests across strain rates and deformation types largely agreed with measurements within experimental uncertainty.
watch_item: Compaction bands can invalidate the homogeneous-deformation assumptions used for calibration, making localization detection important.
paper_title: Large-deformation constitutive modeling of viscoelastic foams: Application to an open-cell foam material
